name: One 97 Communications Ltd
title: One 97 Communications Ltd - 543396 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Paytm's Q4 FY26 call is a consumer-fintech growth story with no capacity signal; net payment margin above 3% and lending distribution are the drivers, but cost step-up is flagged and the transcript is garbled in places.

triggers.label: Net payment margin above 3%
triggers.quote: guidance earlier was greater than three, which is not to say that you're exactly at three

triggers.label: Operating leverage expected; EBITDA margin path 2.5-3 years
triggers.quote: we expect significant operating leverage going forward

triggers.label: Personal loan disbursals restarting
triggers.quote: our personal loan disbursements in the last month

we are guiding for more than 22% growth

prior_guidance_check.metric: Net payment margin greater than 3 bps
prior_guidance_check.quote: guidance earlier was greater than three

evasions.quote: No comments towards any guidance or hint of it.
I'd rather put my head down and execute the journey.
I don't think we've guided that before.

summary.headline: Paytm Q4 FY26: management expects revenue growth to accelerate in FY27 and EBITDA margin to reach 15-20% in two and a half to three years, with no quantified Q4 margin figures in transcript.
summary.overview: Management said payments (about 55% of revenue) and marketing services (about 30%) are the main tailwinds for FY27 acceleration, with personal loans recovering and wealth as a new growth leg. Postpaid disbursal ramp is described as faster than the earlier launch, though no figures were given and management declined to comment on guidance. Net payment margin was about 9 bps, with management pointing to pricing discipline and credit instruments on UPI as drivers. Management said it will spend more on cashback and customer acquisition but within existing guidance, and that new investment will go only into AI, with no material capex plan yet. The company is not pursuing an NBFC licence and says the wallet licence remains a commitment without a timeline.

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: About 55% of revenue; benefiting from offline and UPI credit tailwinds, full payment licence now in place, and rising MDR-bearing instrument mix. Management said MDR-bearing mix growth is lifting net payment margin.

segments.name: Marketing services
segments.commentary: About 30% of revenue; management expects it to contribute to FY27 growth after a drag from a revamp and a headwind in advertising, with management citing a lower base.

segments.name: Financial services (lending distribution)
segments.commentary: Paytm acts as a distribution channel and does not own the loan book; personal loan disbursements recovered in the latest month. Management said wealth/broking is a third leg with low market share, and that retail broking and wealth are targeted for a top-five position.

segments.name: Consumer and merchant sides
segments.commentary: Management said consumer-side and merchant-side profitability was the best in eight quarters. Online merchant GMV is growing and is described as a double-digit share of GMV, not single digit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue growth to accelerate in FY27, with payments and marketing services as the main contributors.
Management expects to reach 15-20% EBITDA margin in two and a half to three years; the analyst's question on the timing received no firm quantified answer.
Management expects significant operating leverage going forward, but declined to give quarter-on-quarter detail.
Cashback and customer-acquisition spend will rise in absolute terms but is said to remain within previously given guidance.
Management said next year's capex will be higher than current levels; this was noted by the analyst as a cash-flow item.
Management said it expects near-full offset of the PIDF subsidy sunset on subscription revenue per device, after achieving a 30-40% offset target in Q4.
capex_capacity: Management said there is no material capex plan yet for AI; any new investment will go only into AI, with the approach of renting data centre capacity and GPUs rather than building.
Management said the company expects capex to rise next year, but gave no figure.
Device base is growing: about 27 lakh devices added, per analyst, with capex per device said to be lower; cohort payback periods are improving.
demand_pricing: Credit-card-on-UPI share of volume is small; management says this share is higher than for standard bank accounts, and Paytm sees no moderation in its own GMV growth.
EMI enablement covers more than half of machines; EMI is used across electronics, healthcare, furniture, fashion, beauty and quick commerce, with a Rs 5,000+ ticket size.
Agentic checkout funnel conversion was described as about 7-8 times higher than the tap-based funnel, per management.
Management said the NBFC licence is not a priority; it prefers the distribution model with multiple lender balance sheets.
Penetration of lending in the merchant base is about 7%, rising about 1% a year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY27 revenue acceleration reflects recovery in services versus broad-based growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payments (about 55% of revenue) and marketing services (about 30%) are the main tailwinds, with personal loans recovering and wealth as a third leg. The exact split was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Postpaid traction versus earlier disbursal peak of about Rs 9,000 Cr a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said traction is better than before and that personal loan disbursements started to recover in the latest month. It gave no figures and declined to comment on guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of net payment margin upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited pricing discipline and the shift to credit instruments on UPI rails, with postpaid starting to contribute; it said a small share of GMV can add 20-40 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did indirect costs rise and what is the operating leverage path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarter-on-quarter changes include appraisal impact; AI-driven efficiencies and an expected acceleration should produce operating leverage. It declined to say whether the path is front- or back-ended.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any impact from the PPBL (Paytm Payments Bank) ban and any wallet or other licence pending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no impact and that the company remains committed to the wallet licence, with no timeline. It said nothing else is pending with RBI.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering an NBFC licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not excited about an NBFC licence and prefers the model of distributing loans across multiple lender balance sheets.

risks_watch: Cashback and marketing spend rising, with management saying spend is measured but not yet tied to MTU gains.
Dependence on PIDF sunset offset and device-based subscription revenue.
Wallet licence has no timeline; PPBL restrictions are a background issue.
Capex step-up next year and AI investment plans, with no quantified figure given.
Margin trajectory to 15-20% EBITDA depends on operating leverage that was not quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and monetisation, with management repeatedly saying progress is better than before. Evasive on quantified targets: management declined to give guidance on postpaid disbursal levels, quarter-by-quarter cost path, and capex size.
key_quotes: Investment is attention and effort, not capital.
Payments is our customer acquisition. This is our monetization layer.

financial_highlights.metric: Net payment margin (as discussed by analyst, adjusted for PIDF)
financial_highlights.value: about 9 bps overall, per analyst; guidance earlier was greater than 3 bps on core basis

financial_highlights.change: up about 1% a year (from about 6% a year ago)

financial_highlights.value: 30-40% offset target; management says it achieved this in Q4 and expects near-full offset

growth.why: Management expects FY27 revenue growth to accelerate, led by payments and marketing services, with net payment margin guidance of greater than 3 bps held and indirect cost growth guided at more than 22%, but no quantified revenue guidance or capacity backing was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-3 quarters, with 15-20% EBITDA margin in 2.5-3 years
rows.why: Management targets 15-20% EBITDA margin in two and a half to three years and cites operating leverage plus net payment margin upside from MDR-bearing mix, but current EBITDA margin is about 6% and no quarterly path was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity plan was discussed; AI compute is to be rented from data centres and GPUs rather than built, and the device base growth (about 27 lakh added) is not tied to a capacity build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects revenue growth to accelerate in FY27 led by payments (about 55% of revenue) and marketing services (about 30%), with personal loan disbursements recovering in the latest month and merchant loan penetration rising about 1% a year from about 7%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex will rise next year but gave no figure, and no material capex plan has been set; utilisation is not a meaningful driver because the model is asset-light.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give quantified guidance on postpaid disbursals, cost path or capex, and kept net payment margin guidance at greater than 3 bps and indirect cost growth at more than 22%, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cashback and customer-acquisition spend will rise in absolute terms, indirect cost growth is guided at more than 22%, and the PIDF subsidy sunset is a dependency for subscription revenue, though management says it achieved a 30-40% offset in Q4 and expects near-full offset.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Postpaid disbursal ramp is described as faster than the earlier launch and wealth/broking is a new growth leg, but no product dates or figures were given.

rows.label: Net payment margin uplift from credit instruments on UPI
rows.why: Management cited pricing discipline and the shift to UPI credit instruments, and said a small share of GMV can add 20-40 bps, against net payment margin of about 9 bps and guidance of greater than 3 bps.

rows.label: Personal loan disbursement recovery
rows.why: Personal loan disbursements recovered in the latest month after the earlier peak of about Rs 9,000 Cr a quarter, though no figures were given.

rows.label: Wallet licence from RBI
rows.why: Management remains committed to the wallet licence but gave no timeline, and the PPBL restrictions are a background issue, so no near-term resolution is signalled.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, monetisation and profitability (consumer and merchant profitability best in eight quarters), but evasive on quantified targets for postpaid disbursals, quarterly cost path and capex size, which analysts pushed on.
